rv.q: That we come to care at all about these brutes is proof of how well Berger and his actors have risen to the challenge of Titus.
In the end, this is about as effective a take on “Titus Andronicus” as you’re likely to see.
Director Jesse Berger never makes a firm commitment in favor of serious tragedy or tongue-in-cheek comedy, resulting in the uncomfortable cohabitation of gasps and guffaws.
Shakespeare devotees will want to encounter this relative stranger because it is unlike anything else in the playwright's catalog.
